mechanism: Core's MaybeDiscourageAndDisconnect has TWO independent exemptions before it punishes anyone (refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:5181-5190): NoBan, and then `if (pnode.IsManualConn()) { LogWarning("Not punishing manually connected peer %d!"); return false; }`. They are independent because a manual connection does NOT get NoBan by default -- CConnman gives an outbound dial NetPermissionFlags::None and consults vWhitelistedRangeOutgoing only for MANUAL connections (refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:510-512), so an -addnode peer with no matching -whitelist ...,out entry holds no permissions at all and is exempt purely by being manual. Our record-misbehavior (src/networking/peer.lisp:1678-1719) has one exemption, peer-has-permission-p +perm-noban+ at :1697, plus Core's loopback carve-out at :1712-1713; peer-manual (the slot at peer.lisp:64) is never consulted in the function, and peer-permission-flags (src/networking/netaddress.lisp:769-806) derives flags from address, direction and onion-ness only, so it cannot report a manual peer as privileged.
consequence: An operator-pinned peer that trips any of the seven misbehaviour sites is disconnected AND its address is added to *discouraged-peers*. connect-peer refuses a discouraged address outright (src/networking/peer.lisp:328-329), and that is the very call connect-added-nodes (src/node/peers.lisp:995) and connect-specified-nodes (:985) make from maintain-peers on every tick, so the redial silently fails from then on. The filter is a 50,000-entry FIFO with no time expiry (src/config.lisp:230-259), so on any node that does not discourage tens of thousands of addresses the entry never rolls out -- the pinned peer is down until the process restarts. That is a stronger outcome than the finding assumed (it expected the filter to forget). It also removes the whole point of -addnode / -connect: the operator's ability to keep a peer whose implementation we disagree with, which is precisely why Core's exemption exists and why Core logs it as a warning rather than acting.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3d, warm image, probe-f.lisp, with *discouraged-peers* and the whitelist specials rebound so the image is not polluted. A manual outbound peer at 203.0.113.7 with no whitelist entry: (:PEER-MANUAL T :HAS-NOBAN NIL) (:RECORD-MISBEHAVIOR-RETURNED T) (:STATE-AFTER :DISCONNECTED :DISCOURAGED T) (:REDIAL-CONNECT-PEER (NIL)) -- punished, and the redial the maintenance loop performs returns NIL. Positive control in the same run, a peer at 203.0.113.8 covered by a noban whitelist entry: (:CONTROL-NOBAN :RETURNED NIL :STATE :READY :DISCOURAGED NIL) -- so the exemption machinery works and what is missing is specifically the manual arm. Ours: src/networking/peer.lisp:1690-1698, :328-329, :64; src/networking/netaddress.lisp:769-806; src/node/peers.lisp:985, :995. Core: refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:5181-5190, refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:510-512.
fix_shape: Add Core's second exemption to record-misbehavior, immediately after the noban one and before discourage-peer: when peer-manual is set, log Core's line ("Not punishing manually connected peer ~A") and return NIL, leaving the connection up and the address untouched -- Core returns false there, so nothing else happens either. Keep it separate from the noban test rather than folding manual into peer-permission-flags: the flags are address-derived and shared with inbound admission and eviction, and granting a manual peer noban would also exempt it from those, which Core does not do. Check the other consumers of the misbehaviour verdict for the same omission while there -- peer.lisp:419 and :741 already consult peer-manual, so the slot is trusted elsewhere. A regression test asserts a manual peer survives record-misbehavior undiscouraged and still connectable, with a non-manual peer at another address in the same run as the positive control.
